name: run_001
why: The deterministic autoplay of the slice as it exists today: title attract, PRESS START, NEW GAME, the crawl, the transition into rm_pp_ship, eight steps of free walk and one NPC dialogue. One clock in steps at 60 a second, no sleeps read from a stopwatch, no key pressed twice because the run took longer than expected. Card DEMO-WALK: the game's own route (data/slice.json) hands the crawl to the drive scene, which owns the screen for 178 seconds and whose twelve caption pages each wait for a press, so this run holds that one route step with PP_ROUTE_HOLD and the run room stands in its place. The video is therefore the run room's walk, which is what the submission describes, and not the drive. A launch with no environment takes the drive exactly as data/slice.json says.
beat_source: knowledge/mechanics/PACING-AND-CUTSCENES.md section 9 (the 32 beat sheet) and ROADMAP-2026-10-22.md section 2 (S1, S2)

game.env_note: PP_ROUTE_HOLD is read by pp_title_crawl_handoff (game/scripts/pp_title/pp_title.gml, card DEMO-WALK) and names the route steps this run does not hand to. It is set here rather than in play_demo.py so the recipe stays in the script, and it stays empty in every launch a player makes.
game.note: the form measured on this PC on 2026-10-21 and recorded in tools/capture_title.py: <game>.exe -game <data>.win is the only form that starts the game instead of opening a file dialog

clock.note: one step is one 60th of a second, which is the game's own step: the GML step event runs at room speed 60, so a step index in this file is the same unit as a step in the game log

seeds.note: title_flash is PP_TITLE_FLASH_SEED (game/scripts/pp_title/pp_title.gml:99), the only random stream this slice reaches: the attract's lightning flashes are drawn from it, so the same launch flashes at the same steps. The encounter and dodge streams (pp_rng_new, game/scripts/pp_rng/pp_rng.gml:8) are not reached by this run, so they are not listed here as if they were pinned.

record.note: 768x720 is exactly 3x the 256x240 NES screen, which is the size the game draws into its window on this PC (measured: a 768x720 viewport at [8, 31] inside a 784x759 window, tests/test_capture_title.py). audio auto means the loopback device when ffmpeg reports one, else a rendered stand-in track that the mp4 and the verify file both label as not the loopback

events.note: title attract: logo, moon, storm cloud, the seeded lightning flash; the recording starts here and no key is pressed, so 10 s of the attract are in the file
PRESS START opens the menu on NEW GAME (the fight song of tools/capture_title.py: enter is the confirm key, game/scripts/pp_input/pp_input.gml)
NEW GAME confirmed, which starts the intro; 1.5 s after the menu press so the menu cursor animation is in the recording

the game's own line that NEW GAME took (written by pp_title when the crawl starts, game/scripts/pp_title/pp_title.gml:841 area). The step is the fallback used when the log is block buffered; the marker only ever moves this note earlier, never later
the crawl's first beats are running; no key is pressed on purpose, because a confirm on the intro finishes the crawl and would delete the beat this run exists to show
crawl beats three and four, still with no key: the reveal machine runs at its own speed (data/intro_text.json, 258 characters over six beats)
crawl beats five and six, the hold before the transition

the game's own line when the crawl ends and the run room loads (pp_title: 'PP title: intro finished, starting the run in rm_pp_ship'). Between the two lines the title plays its 240 step night drive and the fade, which is the whole of beats 7 to 25 in this build. This was a fallback of step 3300 until card t_ec7072b5, and that fallback was the real cause of the dead air at the end of the take: the validator will not let an event be declared before the previous one, so the walk could not be written earlier than 3300 (55.0 s) even though the line lands at 2591 to 2595 on this PC (2591 on demo-walk-2026-10-26.mp4, 2595 on nightly-2026-10-26.mp4, both in their verify files' traces). The line has been seen in every take so far, the fallback is only the block buffered log's answer, and 2620 is late enough for the fade's 12 steps behind a room that loaded at 2595

the deck is up and the walker stands on the spawn tile 2,7. This beat used to be step 3360, which left rm_pp_ship sitting still for fourteen seconds. The judge panel takes six stills twelve seconds apart, so its 42.9 s still and its 55.1 s still were the same picture: nothing on screen had moved yet, and the walk itself did not start until 57.0 s, after five of the six stills had been taken

the walk east, and it starts as soon as the deck is up instead of at 57.0 s. One HOLD of the direction, because the walker walks while the key is down (card PP-FREE-MOVE). The corridor is open from the spawn at 2,7 to the tile before the navy_sailor at 11,7, which is 8 tiles or 128 pixels, and 128 pixels is 64 steps at PP_WALK_SPEED's 2 pixels a step; 72 steps gives the walker a little to spare so he is standing against the sailor when the confirm is pressed, since he cannot walk through him. His feet travel 132 pixels before the sailor's own tile stops them, which is 8 footstep cues at PP_FOOTSTEP_PX's 16, and 8 is the number checks.required_footsteps asks this take for. This beat used to be eight taps of Right, one a second: under the tile walk that was eight tiles, under the free walk it is a couple of pixels a press, and a press shorter than one 60 a second step is never read as held at all, so a take could log no footstep cue (nightly-2026-10-26.mp4 did exactly that)
he has arrived: the hold released at step 2772 against the sailor, and this is the room held still for a moment so the last step of the walk is visible

confirm facing the sailor's tile, the same press tools/capture_title.py --room ship makes. Card t_11f6a125: data/maps/all.json now places the navy_sailor actor at 11,7 of ship_small, one tile ahead of the tile this walk stops on, so the press opens his box (dialogue talk_navy_sailor) instead of nothing. Measured on the 2026-10-26 take (output/demo/demo-talk-2026-10-26.mp4): the game log carries 'PP dialogue: talk_navy_sailor with navy_sailor on ship_small 11,7' and seven 'PP audio: text_blip_b played' lines after the eight footstep lines, and the take's verify file holds failures []

the sailor's second line. The first line is fully revealed by now: 29 characters at PP_TEXT_STEPS_SLOW's 2 steps a character is about 60 steps, and the box opened 300 steps ago, so this press turns the box to line 2 and line 2 types out behind the panel's 55.1 s still

the sailor's third line, turned 700 steps after the second. The press sits between the panel's 55.1 s still and its 67.4 s still for every take length from 71.0 s to 76.0 s, which is the band tests/test_move_hold.py measures, so line 3 is on screen at the last still instead of the same line 2 the fifth still already showed. No press follows this one, because the fifth press on a three line box is the press that closes it and would leave the take ending on a still room again

the deck is held to the end step with the sailor's box up on its third line, so the recording ends on a live box rather than on a still room. Only confirm advances the box and no press follows e21, so the third line is what is on screen to the last frame

checks.footstep_note: the walk at e10 is the only walking this take does, and it is what the judge panel's Demo mark is about. The deck is open from the spawn at 2,7 to the navy_sailor's tile at 11,7, so the feet travel 132 pixels before his own tile stops them, and 132 pixels at PP_FOOTSTEP_PX's 16 is 8 footstep cues. Measured on the 2026-10-26 take that worked (demo-walk-2026-10-26.mp4): its verify file holds footsteps 8 and failures []. Measured on the take that did not (nightly-2026-10-26.mp4): footsteps 0 and 'the game played no footstep cue, so the Right presses did not reach the walk', and it still passed its own verify because the route asked for no footsteps. play_demo --check now fails a take that carries fewer than this number
checks.note: end_step is where the recording stops (71 s): the last note plus one second. palette_share_min and palette_tolerance are the game test on a compressed frame: at least 90 per cent of a frame's pixels must sit within 12 levels of a legal 2C02 colour. It is measured, not guessed: the title, the menu and the crawl score 0.93 to 0.99, rm_pp_ship's own art scores 0.11 because it is drawn in greys the NES cannot output (reported as a finding, not hidden), and a terminal or another window has no 2C02 structure at all. min_on_palette_frames is how many of the seven samples must be on palette for the recording to be called a recording of the game
